s1.where: A white page with a bell picture and the large words "Turn on notifications from Messenger", with two buttons below.
s1.expectation: Messenger is asking me whether I want it to tell me when messages arrive.
s1.cue: The large heading "Turn on notifications from Messenger".

first_pass.why: The heading says in plain words what the page is asking. If I looked away, it would remind me at once.

s2.where: The opening list of my conversations, with the word "messenger" at the top and "Chats" lit up in blue at the bottom.
s2.expectation: I am in Messenger, looking at the list of my conversations with people.
s2.cue: The word "messenger" at the top, and the word "Chats" coloured blue in the row at the bottom.

first_pass.why: The top only tells me which program I am in, not which page of it. I have to look down to the small blue word "Chats" and work out that it is the one picked. If the phone rang, the top of the screen would not remind me what I was doing.
first_pass.solution: Put a plain heading at the top that says "Chats" or "Your conversations", not only the name of the program.

test_cases.task: On the first screen, scroll down two screens, look away and count to ten, name the place; then tap the middle and right items of the bottom row and come back with the left one.
test_cases.real_if: You have to hunt or guess to name the place after the pause.
test_cases.not_real_if: You can name it at once from what is on screen.
test_cases.what_happened: I scrolled the first screen down two screens. When I looked back I saw only a long column of strangers' names with blue "Add friend" buttons, "messenger" at the top, and a small blue "Chats" at the bottom. Nothing there looked like my conversations, so I had to guess that I was still on the chats list. When I tapped "People" and then "Notifications", each page had its name in large letters at the top: "People" and "Notifications". That only showed me how bare the first screen is. Tapping "Chats" took me back, still scrolled down among the strangers.

s2.closing_comment: The other two pages name themselves in large letters; the first screen does not, and once I scrolled it did not even look like my conversations.

s3.where: A white panel slid over from the left with my own name, "Ally Cooper", at the top and a list: Communities, Message requests, Archive, Friend requests, Subscriptions, Facebook Reels and so on.
s3.expectation: Some sort of list of places I could go, opened over the main screen. I think it is a menu, but nothing says so.
s3.cue: My name at the top, and the list of words below it.

first_pass.why: The heading is my own name. That tells me whose account it is, not where I am. Nothing says "Menu". I can read every line in the list, but if I looked away I would not know how this panel came to be open or how to put it away.
first_pass.solution: A heading such as "Menu" at the top of the panel, and a plainly labelled "Close" button.

test_cases.task: Open the side panel with the three lines, read it, close it with Back; open it again from the middle item of the bottom row and look again.
test_cases.real_if: The panel never names itself and never marks where you came from.
test_cases.not_real_if: Something on it tells you what it is and where you are.
test_cases.what_happened: I opened the panel from the first screen and later from the Notifications page. Both times it looked exactly the same: my name "Ally Cooper" at the top, then Communities, Message requests, Archive and so on. Nothing says "Menu", and nothing marks Chats or Notifications as where I had come from. Back closed it without trouble.

s3.closing_comment: The panel opens and closes easily, but it never tells me what it is or where I came from.
